body:
> Observed 2026-08-29 on the web board: every running card's log panel shows the same four lines — `# … launch background agent for #162 attempt 1`, `backgrounded · e381f784 · …`, then the `claude agents / attach / logs / stop` hints. 0.4 KB, and nothing about what the worker is doing.

## Why

`.kanban/logs/<n>-<k>.log` is the stdout of the command the dispatcher spawned (`spawnWorker`, `src/dispatch.js`). On `claude` and `claude-track` that command is `claude --bg …`: it asks the session daemon to start the agent, prints the banner, and exits. The worker then lives inside the daemon and writes to Claude Code's own records — `~/.claude/jobs/<id>/state.json` and the transcript under `~/.claude/projects/` — never back into hkb's file (`docs/harnesses.md`: *"a launch banner and nothing else"*). Only `claude-p`, a real child, writes its turns and its final JSON there.

So the panel (`src/serve.js` log endpoint → `web/index.html` drawer; the same tail `hkb show` does not print at all) is honest about the file and useless about the worker. The facts it should show already exist locally, since #137: the attempt row carries `job`, `session_id` and `transcript_path` one tick after launch, and the job record has `detail` — the worker's own one-line status, the text `claude agents` shows — plus `state` and `updatedAt`. `claude logs <id>` is the interactive equivalent and #149 already records that it fails from a sandboxed shell, so reading the record is the right primitive for both surfaces.

## What

- **`jobs.js`**: one function, `attemptActivity(attempt)` → `{state, detail, updated_at, last_message, transcript_lines}` from `readJobState` (already there) plus the transcript's last assistant text block (last N lines of `transcript_path`, parsed with the same care `parseTranscriptUsage` takes — never throw, null when absent). Two local reads, no subprocess.
- **`hkb show <n>`** prints, for a live `--bg` attempt: `working · <detail> · last turn <age>` and the last assistant message indented under it; for an ended one, the outcome line it prints today. `--json`: `attempts[].activity`.
- **The drawer** shows the same block above the file tail, with the banner demoted to one `launched <when> · job <id>` line. For `claude-p` and Copilot/Codex attempts (a real child), the file tail stays the primary view — it is the worker's output there.
- **Freshness**: the drawer already polls; `activity` rides the payload it fetches, no new request. The transcript read is capped (tail bytes, like `tailLog`) so a long session costs the same as a short one.

## Constraints

- Never a subprocess (no `claude logs`); never an API call. Both records are files on the host that launched the attempt, so a board viewed from another machine shows the file tail and says so.
- Nothing here changes what is recorded; it only shows what #137 already stamps.

## Done when

- A running `claude` attempt shows its `detail` and last message in `hkb show` and the drawer; the launch banner is one line.
- A `claude-p` attempt is unchanged; a board with no job record for an attempt shows the file tail with no error.
- `test/jobs.test.js` (activity from a fixture job + transcript, and from nothing), `test/serve.test.js`, `test/cli.test.js`; `npm run lint && npm test` green.
title: The log panel shows a --bg worker's launch banner; show the job's status line and transcript tail instead
